messages:
maria: Heads-up — found an old .vault-token baked into an internal runner image layer (registry path: gcr.redwood-infra/builds/runner-cache:2024-11-03). It was included in a snapshot we shared with partner X last week. Token looks like a long-lived service token with ability to write to secret/data/staging/* — not publicly indexed but accessible by partner org.

devsec-bot: Automated alert: secret artifact detected in image metadata by image-scan (rule: vault-token-file). Severity: high. Link: https://scans.redwood/alerts/9842

jonathan: ugh. Do we know which Vault token ID it is (token string redacted in logs)? Any bound metadata (policies, creation accessor)?

maria: I grabbed the token accessor and a policy excerpt from the image: accessor=va.9b3f..., policy=stage-service-write. Looks like it was issued by a CI role (ci-runner-role) — created in 2023 and had a long TTL (`ttl: 768h`).

alex: Priority: revoke token immediately, rotate any SA keys that token could impersonate, and search audit logs for usage. I can take revoke + search. @maria can you DM me the accessor and the image digest? I'll run the revoke and query.

maria: sending details to alex now. image digest: sha256:6f8b...; accessor sent via DM.

alex: Plan:
1) vault token-revoke (by accessor) -> `vault token revoke -accessor va.9b3f...`
2) run audit query for accessor & token usage -> `jq` queries on audit log buckets
3) list any secrets written/read under secret/data/staging/* and snapshot accessors
4) rotate any associated GCP SA keys referenced in the CI pipeline
5) update pipeline to stop baking tokens into images and issue ephemeral tokens via workload identity

jonathan: Quick Q on KMS/Vault integration: does this token leak force a rewrap/rotation of our KMS keys that back the transit engine? Or is revoking token + rotating SA keys sufficient?

kate: From my read: the token itself isn't a KMS-wrapped secret. The vault data in KV may be encrypted using Vault's master key (stored in Vault core), and if we use Cloud KMS for auto-unseal, that KMS key is sensitive *only* if its raw key material is exposed. A token leak does NOT by itself require rekeying/unsealing key rotation unless we have evidence someone extracted unseal keys or the KMS key itself. So start with token revoke + audit. If audit shows unauthorized reads of encrypted values, consider rekey/rewrap.

infra: Also worth checking if any IaC templates in repo created static tokens during image build — we should patch those and deploy a rolling rebuild of affected images.

maria: I've opened a short-lived incident page: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2024-212 — tagging SRE and infra. Action owners below.

alex: Executed revoke: `vault token revoke -accessor va.9b3f...` — command returned 204. Running audit search now (querying last 90 days across audit-backup-logs). Early results: two uses from runner IPs to read secret/data/staging/config (timestamps within last 30d). Will list exact paths and create a CSV.

sre-oncall: Recommend setting temporary rate-limits and blocklisting the image digest in registry to prevent further pulls while we triage. I can block image digest — doing it now.

jonathan: For rotation, propose this sequence (minimal blast radius):
- revoke token (done)
- rotate any SA keys referenced by the CI role (create new keys, update CI secrets)
- force rotate any Vault static secrets under secret/data/staging/* (write new values, bump versions)
- add short-lived policy/role for CI with TTL <= 1h and switch pipeline to use Vault Agent or OIDC
- enable or verify audit logging retention and export to BigQuery for long-term forensic

kate: Agree. Also: recommend creating a scoped Vault role that issues tokens with `num_uses` and short `ttl` for build agents. Update docs + add a pre-commit hook that fails if a token file is present in image context.

maria: Owners & timeline:
- alex: audit search & list of affected secrets (ETA 2h)
- infra: block image digest + schedule rebuild (ETA 30m to block, rebuild ETA 6h)
- jonathan: update CI to OIDC/short TTL role, prepare TF changes (ETA 24h)
- kate: policy + pre-commit hook + docs (ETA 48h)

devsec-bot: Checklist generated: [revoke-token, audit-query, rotate-sa-keys, rotate-secrets, block-image, rebuild-images, enforce-ci-ephemeral, add-audit-retention].

alex: Audit results attached (summary): Found 2 read operations and 0 writes from the exposed accessor. Secrets read: secret/data/staging/config (version 3) and secret/data/staging/feature-flag (v1). No evidence of exfil beyond reads. I'll rotate both secrets: writing new values and incrementing versions.

maria: Rotating secrets now. After rotate I'll post confirmation and a note with PRs for pipeline changes.

infra: Image digest blocked in registry and in CD pipeline to prevent future deployments. Rebuild jobs queued.

kate: Created PR: https://git.redwood/policies/ci-token-hardening/pull/12 — adds pre-commit hook and CI check to fail on token artifacts. Also PR to create new Vault role with ttl 1h: https://git.redwood/vault-configs/pull/45

sre-oncall: Confirmed audit logging capture includes the accessor events; exported to bq dataset inc_2024_212 for retention.

maria: Update — secrets rotated, token revoked, image blocked. No further reads since block. Thanks everyone. I'll keep the incident open until rebuilds & CI switch are live. :white_check_mark:

alex: follow-up: schedule a quick retro on lessons and add image-scan rule to fail builds if `.vault-token` present. Also recommend rotating any other long-lived tokens older than 6 months.

maria: Agreed. Closing loop: postmortem to infra and sec weekly, but incident will remain open until CI migration is complete.

devsec-bot: Incident INC-2024-212 status: mitigated -> monitoring. ETA for closure: 2024-11-10.
